feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within NACo strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good impact evidence: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and tool stack details make achievements believable.  
- Strong positioning for target roles: summary, competencies, and experience consistently support digital strategy, platform modernization, and cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Strengthen impact language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes (“support,” “advise,” “helped improve”). Add clearer results, scale, or business value where possible.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); consider “cross-channel communications” vs “multi-channel communication” for consistency. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specific positioning, cleaner phrasing, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for grammar and brevity.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and sector fit: public-sector/advocacy, mission-driven organizations, and digital transformation.
- Tighten the channel list so it reads less like a skills inventory and more like an executive summary.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Skilled at stakeholder coordination and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already well evidenced in the NACo experience, so keep it concise here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad or duplicated phrases with sharper, leadership-level terms: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “CMS modernization,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Standardize wording for parallel structure; e.g., use noun phrases throughout and change “Multi-channel communication” to “Multichannel communications.”
- Consider a tighter version: Digital transformation strategy • Multichannel communications • CMS administration & modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Use “cross-functional” instead of “cross-department” for a more modern, broadly applicable tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially digital strategy, analytics, multimedia, and workflow/systems themes.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 highest-impact contributions and add outcomes where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-led statements, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing toolkits.
- Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, search success, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level or remove one layer of detail.
- “Governance/workflows/analytics” repeats prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep metrics together: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-oriented: add growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed here as building enterprise capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level and emphasize operational scale, editorial coordination, and channel-building.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show creation/scale: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”  
  If possible, add metrics: send volume, open/click rates, video cadence/views, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director entry; keep this role more execution/operations-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify how this role expanded or formalized the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, less repetitive wording:  
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations  
- Editorial governance and content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Advocacy and mission-driven messaging  
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets to improve scanability and avoid sounding like a repeat of “Core Competencies.”
- Use “content operations” or “content strategy” instead of “content planning,” which feels less senior.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable impact for experience bullets rather than skills lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate the Core Competencies section almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats positioning already established in the header and NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills block, make it more strategic, grouped, and tied to the candidate’s most recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and CMS modernization” instead of separate fragmented items.
- Prioritize recent/relevant strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search; de-emphasize older or less central platforms.
- Tighten wording and group related items: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)” and “Workflow automation and Airtable systems.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages • CMS modernization and front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing in both places.
- Most tools are duplicated in “Technical + IT,” so keep this section higher-level and not exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a software inventory rather than a senior capability statement. Since the NACo role already proves the stack, this item should emphasize decision-making, reporting, and optimization outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than a pure platform list.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support” for stronger senior-level language.
- Optional rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding & decision support • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tools list.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational scope and leadership-level delivery rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality multimedia production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to sound more senior.
- Use parallel phrasing and reduce filler; “Livestreaming” → “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” is clearer and more outcome-oriented.
- If space allows elsewhere, move tool-specific detail like PTZ/studio workflows to Technical + IT and keep this section focused on strategic production capability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and livestream workflows are also echoed in Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows”).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should emphasize platform depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than read as a simple tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency/context instead of a bare list, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more specific to match recent impact: **Drupal 9/10** rather than just Drupal.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the richer detail in one place and make this version shorter.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms; remove it unless it supports a project you want to highlight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • **Tagging & tracking:** Google Tag Manager
- Drop version numbers unless required; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- Consider replacing broad terms with stronger phrasing if accurate: “REST/API integrations,” “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers),” “CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions).”
- If possible, connect to outcomes elsewhere in the CV rather than here; this section should stay concise and tool-focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions unless differentiated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Make it more strategic by grouping tools by function and emphasizing the platforms most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped categories for clarity: “Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first: keep Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier prominent because they align with recent workflow/operations work.
- Consider trimming weaker or older tools if space is tight; 6–7 tools is usually enough for this type of skills line.
- If accurate, add a qualifier in another section rather than here, e.g., “built workflow automations and cross-team planning systems,” since outcomes matter more than listing every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are generic collaboration tools; they add less value than automation/project systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the recent leadership over email channels, but it’s currently just a vendor list. Make it sharper and more senior by signaling function and avoiding overlap with broader “multi-channel communications” claims elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light functional context: **Email marketing, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and engagement workflows**
- Keep only platforms you’ve directly administered or used strategically; order by strongest/recentest experience

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps somewhat with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; don’t repeat outcomes here unless you remove them from role descriptions
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate Higher Logic’s community/member-engagement implications without adding clarity

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any scale/results you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope/results where possible: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email audience, or workflow/time savings from the website refresh.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked verbs: replace “supporting the creation… and strengthening workflows” with one concrete outcome per clause.
- Example: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize multi-channel publishing workflows while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the launch/early production phase.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; produced digital and multimedia content to extend member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and foreground ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to” and “supporting organizational programs” with stronger verbs: coordinated, produced, launched, led.
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience/listens, stakeholder groups served, or types/volume of research projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, and channel leadership in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “multimedia production” language too heavily unless tied to the podcast or research/program support.
